newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissho Iwai invests in NZ lithium carbonate maker.
newsitem.headline: Nissho Iwai invests in NZ lithium carbonate maker.

text.p: Japanese trading company Nissho Iwai Corp said on Wedneday that it had invested about 200 million yen in Pacific Lithium Ltd of New Zealand, which developed a new way to make lithium carbonate.
Lithium carbonate is used in products such as lithium batteries, glass and enamel.
The New Zealand company developed a way to make lithium carbonate from sea water, Nissho Iwai said.
The company aims to start operating a plant near Auckland to produce lithium carbonate at an annual rate of 3,000 tonnes from the spring of 1997, Nissho Iwai said.
Pacific Lithium plans to become the first company in the world to make lithium carbonate from sea water, Nissho Iwai said.
Nissho Iwai plans to become a wholesaler for Pacific Lithium for the global market, it said.

The New Zealand firm is 50 percent owned by the company's directors, about 31 percent by individual investors, about 10 percent by Vertex Pte Ltd, an investment company in Singapore, and 8.34 percent by Nissho Iwai, Nissho Iwai said.
